comparison: Perfect alignment on clinical findings (C1-C8, C72-C73). Both evaluations find strong support from multiple datasets and patient samples. OpenEval emphasizes convergence across >1000 patients and multiple cohorts; peer reviewers describe evidence as 'solid,' 'valuable,' and part of a 'comprehensive study.'

Complete agreement on functional effects (C9-C14). Both evaluations support RBM7's role in metastasis through in vivo models and multiple assays. OpenEval highlights complementary gain/loss-of-function approaches; peer reviewers find animal model results 'impressive' with 'consistent and convincing' evidence.

Full concordance on splicing regulation (C15-C22, C68). Both evaluations support RBM7 as a splicing activator. OpenEval details RNA-seq analysis showing ~70% SE/A5E events with decreased PSI; peer reviewers acknowledge 'novel role of RBM7 in controlling alternative splicing' with no methodological concerns.

Strong agreement on MFGE8 as direct target (C23-C31). Both evaluations support mechanistic evidence from RIP-seq, minigene assays, and motif binding. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of independent methods; peer reviewers commend 'in-depth mechanistic study' and accept direct binding evidence without question.

Complete alignment on MFGE8 isoform functions (C32-C40, C76-C77). Both evaluations support opposing roles of L/S isoforms through multiple functional assays. OpenEval highlights STAT1 signaling link; peer reviewers find evidence 'consistent and convincing' for the splicing switch and regulatory pathway.

Full agreement on rescue experiments (C41-C42, C51). Both evaluations support causality through MFGE8-L restoration and ASO experiments. OpenEval emphasizes complementary gain/loss-of-function approaches; peer reviewers accept these as part of comprehensive evidence establishing the mechanistic link.

Strong concordance on dual mechanism (C43-C50, C67, C78). Both evaluations support MFGE8-independent NF-κB pathway. OpenEval details GSEA, western blots, and pharmacological inhibition; peer reviewers describe the RBM7-MFGE8-NF-κB regulatory cascade as 'consistent and convincing.'

Complete agreement on clinical validation (C52-C57). Both evaluations support MFGE8 splicing switch relevance through TCGA analysis and patient samples. OpenEval emphasizes consistency between database and direct measurements; peer reviewers accept clinical data as 'solid' and of 'broad interest to clinicians.'

Strong alignment on SF3B2 interaction (C58-C59, C69-C71). Both evaluations support cooperative mechanism through co-IP and similar splicing phenotypes. OpenEval notes C70 (mutually exclusive binding) is inferred rather than directly demonstrated; peer reviewers accept the splicing mechanism without concerns. Note: OpenEval includes C62 while peer review does not.

High overlap on background claims (C60-C66, C81-C92). Both evaluations support these as appropriate contextual citations. OpenEval characterizes these as background statements from literature; peer reviewers implicitly accept the foundation, noting the study builds on this to address emerging directions. Note: OpenEval includes C62 which peer review places elsewhere.

Strong agreement on overall conclusions (C75, C79-C80). Both evaluations support main findings and therapeutic potential. OpenEval notes C80 is speculative but reasonable; peer reviewers explicitly endorse 'potentially new prognostic and therapeutic target' with conclusions 'supported by many lines of evidence.' Note: C74 appears in OpenEval R11 but peer R11.
